topic: Sharp selection-relevance modulus and tie-uniform inference for Yang–Li–Wu’s generated influence-ranked all-top-k external-control selector: define the sharp modulus omega*(delta) comparing root-n ATE-coordinate distance with leading MSE-criterion distance; prove exact-tie invariance and its sharp near-zero order or refute it with an explicit legal nested-prefix counterexample; translate the answer into the correct local-gap selected-estimator law and a computable multiplier interval uniformly valid across fixed, vanishing, and exact gaps.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp selection-relevance modulus omega*(delta), defined as the largest root-n ATE-coordinate separation between two legal influence-ranked nested prefixes whose leading MSE criteria differ by at most delta, including whether omega*(0)=0 and the exact near-zero order, or refute tie invariance with an explicit legal finite-support counterexample.

source_refs.claim: The population-optimal set may contain multiple MSE-minimizing prefixes, but selection consistency is proved only under a fixed positive MSE separation eta.
source_refs.author: Qinwei Yang, Jingyi Li, Peng Wu, Shu Yang

source_refs.claim: At nondifferentiable boundaries such as ties, the ordinary bootstrap can fail; valid resampling must estimate and apply the directional derivative.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang, Andres Santos

source_refs.excerpt: For the transfer theorem, exhibit one concrete original experiment whose sample split verifies gamma_n and alpha_n
The deterministic known-radius selector attains the three-branch upper benchmark for every alphabet.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yang et al. explicitly allow multiple population MSE minimizers, while their Theorem 3 conditions on a given influence ranking and assumes every nonoptimal prefix is separated by a fixed eta. Their fixed-prefix CLT and pointwise MSE rate do not control how close two prefixes' ATE coordinates must be when their leading criteria tie or nearly tie. The banked asymmetric-game result likewise leaves transfer conditional on abstract approximation errors, and the discrete-ATE construction uses a deterministic known-radius selector rather than a generated ordering. Here both the order and criterion are estimated from correlated influence-function coordinates, so the missing first step is a uniform prefix-EIF coercivity inequality over the legal model class; an unconstrained Gaussian example cannot settle it. The suggested Gaussian diagonal/antidiagonal rigidity and linear no-X Uniform modulus therefore remain hypotheses to prove sharply or refute with a legal nested-prefix law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp theorem giving omega*(delta)=Theta(delta^alpha) with matching legal witnesses, omega*(0)=0, and a characterization of admissible exact ties, or a finite-support RCT/external-control law with two or three legal nested prefixes having equal leading MSE but distinct root-n ATE coordinates.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact external-control estimand, generated influence ranking, nested-prefix selector, and fixed-gap theorem whose proof boundary is being closed.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Small RCTs invite external-control borrowing -> heterogeneous controls create a bias-variance tradeoff -> influence scores generate nested top-k candidates and estimated MSE selects one -> ties and local MSE gaps require a sharp link from criterion proximity to ATE proximity.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute the directional derivative of a minimum or argmin-related functional at a multi-minimizer point and use derivative-aware resampling rather than the ordinary bootstrap.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The modulus is the selector-specific regularity condition determining whether the nonsmooth selection map is harmless at a tie.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand focus-specific mean squared error under local misspecification and compare competing estimators through their joint local-risk coordinates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Yang et al.'s rule is a causal, prefix-indexed focused-MSE selector, so the local-risk expansion is the natural donor calculation for the near-zero modulus.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish, or disprove by a sign-changing finite-support construction, a uniform joint asymptotic linearization and prefix-EIF coercivity result for all top-k ATE and MSE coordinates when the prefix order is generated from Yang et al.'s estimated influence scores with covariates.

source_refs.claim: Influence scores use the RCT-fitted outcome-model parameter and Hessian, yet the MSE theorem is stated for any given borrowed set and the validity theorem conditions on a given ranking.
source_refs.author: Qinwei Yang, Jingyi Li, Peng Wu, Shu Yang

source_refs.claim: Inference for estimated sorted effects requires dedicated differentiability results for sorting and classification operators.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Ivan Fernandez-Val, Ye Luo

source_refs.claim: Cross-fitting and Neyman-orthogonal scores yield root-n causal inference with learned nuisances, but do not by themselves regularize a discontinuous estimated sorting map.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Mert Demirer, Esther Duflo, Christian Hansen, Whitney Newey, James Robins

source_refs.claim: Estimated rankings carry substantial uncertainty, and naive bootstrap rank inference can fail in the presence of ties.
source_refs.author: Magne Mogstad, Joseph P. Romano, Azeem M. Shaikh, Daniel Wilhelm

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yang et al.'s score is generated from the same RCT controls through an empirical-risk minimizer and inverse Hessian, after which all external controls are sorted and every prefix is refitted. Their pointwise proof for a fixed borrowed set neither controls rank switches nor yields a supremum remainder over prefixes, and it does not justify replacing a population prefix by a stochastic top-k prefix. Cross-fitting handles smooth nuisance leakage, whereas sorting needs separate regularity near score level sets; exact and local score ties are where that step fails. With covariates, cancellation and sign changes in prefix EIFs may also defeat the coercivity needed to translate criterion gaps into ATE-coordinate gaps.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving a uniform influence-function expansion and consistent joint covariance estimate for every stochastic top-k prefix, plus a lower bound linking prefix EIF distance to leading-MSE distance under explicit score-margin and covariate-overlap conditions, or a legal finite-support covariate model violating that bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It defines the generated influence score and nested-prefix workflow, while its fixed-ranking theorem pinpoints the unresolved transition.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Influence scores estimate individual external-control comparability -> estimated scores induce a complete nested-prefix path -> every candidate ATE and MSE is evaluated on that path -> valid selection inference requires uniform control of the generated ordering and all prefix EIFs.

method_exemplars.technique: Establish Hadamard differentiability of sorting and classification operators and bootstrap the resulting sorted process.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The first nonsmooth operation in Yang et al.'s pipeline is sorting estimated, covariate-dependent influence scores.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fit nuisance estimates, exploit orthogonal score expansions, and control product-rate remainders uniformly.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After ranking instability is isolated, each prefix ATE is an orthogonal semiparametric estimator with learned outcome and sampling-score nuisances.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert simultaneous pairwise comparisons to obtain rank confidence sets that remain valid with ties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Pairwise influence-score comparisons determine which external-control observations can enter each stochastic prefix.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive the local-gap weak limit of Yang et al.'s selected ATE estimator when prefix MSE gaps are fixed, vanish at the criterion-noise rate, or are exactly zero, allowing arbitrary covariance between candidate ATE influence functions and estimated-MSE coordinates.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves asymptotic normality for each given borrowed set and consistency of the selected prefix only under fixed positive separation; it does not give the selected estimator's boundary law.
source_refs.author: Qinwei Yang, Jingyi Li, Peng Wu, Shu Yang

source_refs.claim: Post-selection estimator distributions generally cannot be estimated uniformly, even locally, without additional structure resolving near-boundary behavior.
source_refs.author: Hannes Leeb, Benedikt M. Poetscher

source_refs.claim: Focused information criteria compare estimator-specific MSE under local misspecification, producing non-oracle selection behavior at local alternatives.
source_refs.author: Gerda Claeskens, Nils Lid Hjort
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: under a local gap a/sqrt n the estimator limit is max{Z_0,Z_1-a}.
The asymptotic version must still check covariance estimation, event approximation, and uniformity near ties.
Replace the failure-only kernel with a new calibration or correction rule for the contact-gap endpoint

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yang et al.'s Theorem 1 centers each candidate estimator at a prefix-specific bias, Theorem 2 controls estimated MSE only for a given prefix, and Theorem 3 removes selection by imposing fixed eta separation. At criterion gaps comparable to MSE-estimation noise, the selected index stays random and is correlated with every candidate ATE coordinate because both use the same observations. The banked bound-intersection attempt confirms that a bare two-coordinate local max law is generic rather than new, while the IDA attempt records the model-specific missing pieces: covariance estimation, selection-event approximation, and uniformity near ties. Leeb and Poetscher rule out a naive uniformly reliable plug-in post-selection law in general; a positive theorem here must exploit the legal nested-prefix covariance and the tie invariance, if any, delivered by the sharp modulus.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular-array theorem representing root-n times the selected ATE error as the ATE coordinate of a jointly Gaussian vector indexed by the argmin of drifted Gaussian criterion coordinates, with explicit reductions to an oracle normal law for fixed gaps and a tie-mixture or invariant law for exact gaps.

writing_exemplar.why: Its fixed-prefix CLT and fixed-gap selection result make the missing local asymptotic regime transparent.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Each borrowed prefix has an asymptotically linear ATE estimator -> estimated MSE selects among correlated prefixes -> fixed separation makes selection asymptotically deterministic -> local and zero gaps instead produce a correlated Gaussian argmin law.

method_exemplars.technique: Use local-misspecification expansions to obtain joint limiting risk criteria and then apply the random model-selection map to the corresponding focus estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems select an estimator by estimated MSE for one target and become nonregular when population risks are locally indistinguishable.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply a directional delta method at nonunique minima and characterize when a Gaussian plug-in bootstrap fails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The exact-gap selected coordinate is a nonsmooth function of a joint Gaussian ATE-and-criterion vector.

method_exemplars.technique: Localize the active argmax set and approximate its Gaussian supremum uniformly over changing contact sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The near-minimizing prefix set is the finite-selector analogue of a changing contact set.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a computable multiplier confidence interval for the ATE reported after Yang et al.'s MSE-minimizing prefix selection that has uniform coverage over fixed, vanishing, and exact prefix gaps while shrinking toward the oracle interval when the winning prefix is well separated.

source_refs.claim: The proposed workflow reports the estimator from the estimated-MSE-minimizing prefix, but its theory supplies no selection-adjusted confidence interval at multiple or near-multiple minima.
source_refs.author: Qinwei Yang, Jingyi Li, Peng Wu, Shu Yang

source_refs.claim: Inference on a target chosen through optimization requires winner's-curse correction; conditional and hybrid projection intervals can remain informative.
source_refs.author: Isaiah Andrews, Toru Kitagawa, Adam McCloskey

source_refs.claim: Gaussian and bootstrap approximations for maxima of high-dimensional sample-mean vectors allow arbitrary coordinate correlation.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Kengo Kato, Yuta Koike

source_refs.claim: Locally simultaneous inference protects all plausibly selected targets and adapts toward ordinary inference when only one target could plausibly win.
source_refs.author: Tijana Zrnic, William Fithian

source_refs.claim: Conformal selective borrowing gives finite-sample randomization inference with selection uncertainty, but does not derive a superpopulation ATE interval for the influence-ranked prefix selector.
source_refs.author: Ke Zhu, Shu Yang, Xiaofei Wang

source_refs.excerpt: explicit multiplier critical-value construction with stated rates for a_n and eta_n
The matching union-honest upper interval and exact expected-length frontier remain open

open_problems.why_unsolved: A direct Wald interval for the chosen prefix ignores the covariance between selection noise and ATE noise. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey handle targets selected directly by optimizing estimated effects, while Yang et al. minimize a quadratic MSE estimate built from a fused-versus-trial estimator difference and a variance estimate; the event is therefore not the standard winner event and its coordinates are generated by estimated ranks and nuisances. The banked partial-transport review asks for an explicit multiplier critical value with tolerance rates, and the banked optimal-value result leaves its matching union-honest interval and length frontier open. CCK and locally simultaneous inference provide the coupling and adaptive architecture, while Zhu et al. establish a different design-based randomization result, but none proves a superpopulation interval for this causal nested-prefix selector.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit multiplier algorithm jointly resampling prefix ATE and MSE influence coordinates, forming a data-dependent set of plausible minimizers, and returning an interval whose infimal triangular-array coverage is at least 1-alpha across all gap regimes, with oracle-width equivalence under fixed separation and a nonvacuous exact-tie length guarantee.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly explains why optimization-induced target selection invalidates conventional intervals and how conditional or projection hybrids restore validity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Researchers choose among noisy alternatives -> optimization selects favorable noise as well as signal -> conventional uncertainty for the selected target undercovers -> a selection-aware interval is needed for the ATE attached to the MSE-winning prefix.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine conditional Gaussian inference for a selected coordinate with projection protection to obtain a hybrid interval.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is inference on one causal-effect coordinate selected from a correlated finite vector by optimization.

method_exemplars.technique: Screen a locally plausible selection set using one error budget and conduct simultaneous inference over that set using the remaining budget.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A plausible-prefix set can adapt continuously from all tied prefixes to a singleton under a fixed MSE gap.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian anti-concentration and multiplier-bootstrap coupling for maxima of correlated high-dimensional score vectors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The interval must control simultaneous errors over many strongly correlated nested prefixes without assuming nonsingular covariance.

literature_map:
Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang (2026, arXiv:2604.13973) introduce the generated influence ranking and all-top-k MSE selector; Theorem 2 is pointwise for a given prefix and Theorem 3 requires fixed eta separation.
Li, Miao, Lu, and Zhou (2023, Biometrics, doi:10.1111/biom.13583) derive efficient and doubly robust ATE estimation when external controls satisfy mean exchangeability.
Gao, Yang, Shan, Ye, Lipkovich, and Faries (2025, Biometrika, doi:10.1093/biomet/asae069) use adaptive-lasso bias penalization for selective borrowing and give inference under their selection conditions.
Valancius et al. (2024, Biometrics, doi:10.1093/biomtc/ujae095) formalize causal assumptions and efficient influence functions for hybrid trials, but not an MSE-selected random prefix.
Zhu, Yang, and Wang (2025, ICML, arXiv:2410.11713) incorporate selection uncertainty into finite-sample randomization inference, a distinct design-based target.
Claeskens and Hjort (2003, JASA, doi:10.1198/016214503000000819) provide the closest local-MSE model-selection expansion, but not for generated causal prefixes.
Leeb and Poetscher (2008, Econometric Theory, arXiv:0704.1584) show post-selection distributions are generally not uniformly estimable, making selector-specific structure essential.
Fang and Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:1404.3763) show ordinary bootstrap failure at directionally differentiable boundaries and provide derivative-aware resampling.
Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey (2024, QJE, doi:10.1093/qje/qjad043) develop conditional and hybrid inference for optimization-selected targets.
Zrnic and Fithian (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2212.09009) give locally simultaneous inference adapting between singleton and multiple plausible winners.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1912.10529) supply multiplier-bootstrap coupling for maxima with arbitrary coordinate dependence.
Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm (2024, Review of Economic Studies, doi:10.1093/restud/rdad006) develop rank confidence sets robust to ties.
Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Luo (2018, Econometrica, arXiv:1512.05635) derive differentiability and bootstrap theory for estimated sorting operators.
Chernozhukov et al. (2018, The Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) provide cross-fitted orthogonal causal-score theory, but smooth nuisance robustness does not control rank switches.
No located paper gives the target combination: a sharp MSE-to-ATE modulus, local-gap Gaussian argmin law, and tie-uniform multiplier interval for an influence-generated nested external-control prefix.
